what: The seam conventions' known answers, worked by hand by the lead on 2026-11-23, with the sums written out. Nothing here was produced by the model or by the statistics package. docs/model/conventions.md states the conventions; tests/test_seam_conventions.py holds the model and the statistics package to these answers.

one_channel.note: Convention (b): score[i] = c[0]*x[i-2] + c[1]*x[i-1] + c[2]*x[i], a sample before the stream's start taken as zero. A pulse 1, 2, 3 whose first sample is at index 2, in seven frames.
one_channel.peak_is: index of the pulse's first sample, 2, plus taps - 1, 2: convention (a) with (b)

wrong_way_round.note: The same sums with the coefficients newest sample first, 3, 2, 1: the convolution form's reading of the same list. The answer convention (b) rules out.

crossing.note: Convention (c): a crossing is a score strictly greater than the threshold. On the scores above.
crossing.why: Above 13: only 14, at index 4. Above 7: 8, 14, 8 at indexes 3, 4, 5, one run, so one rising crossing at 3. Above 2: 3, 8, 14, 8, 3 at indexes 2 to 6, one run, rising at 2.

two_channels.note: Convention (d): a filter's output is the sum over the channels it reads. Channel a carries the one-channel case above under its row 1, 2, 3. Channel b carries 0, 5, 0, 0, 1, 0, 0 under the row 2, 0, 1.
two_channels.scores_are: the one-channel scores 0, 0, 3, 8, 14, 8, 3 plus b's, index by index

tie_set.note: The quantising rule, on a set where every value but the peak lands on a tie. The peak 262142 maps to 131071 = 2^17 - 1, so each value is halved: 1/2, 3/2, 5/2, -1/2, -3/2. Half to even gives 0, 2, 2, 0, -2. Half away from zero, the wrong rule, gives 1, 2, 3, -1, -2.
